feat: fnGlobalObject.js joins the ported harness includes - the stock body Function("return this;")() now runs on tr and answers the G2 globalThis singleton (the this-rewrite knife), so the port returns the singleton directly (an equivalence reduction, not a stand-in: the rotation-366 no-backdoor constraint dissolved the moment the substrate ran the real shape); runner whitelists the include and rewrites fnGlobalObject( call sites to __t262_fnGlobalObject(, the tree-shake reaches the new segment lexically, and the stale no-expression-surface note in the harness header is corrected - 130 include cases enter the truly-run surface

feat: a dynamic function's this binds to the global object - the function_ctor touches-this gate turns from a loud reject into the 10.2.1.2 rewrite (a sloppy function called with an undefined thisArg binds this to the global object per OrdinaryCallBindThis step 5.a.ii, and tr mints exactly one - the G2 globalThis singleton - so every This in the synthesized body rewrites to the globalThis ident and answers the same object; the fnGlobalObject harness body Function("return this;")() is exactly this shape). The gate narrows instead of vanishing: a strict-prologue body keeps the reject (strict this is undefined, a different rewrite with no measured demand), and a body whose token stream carries the function keyword keeps it too (a nested function owns its own this and the flat arena scan cannot tell whose this it sees - body_lexes_fn_keyword, same token-level judgement as the bare-with scan; a true arrow pierces this per 8.3.4 and does not disqualify). fixture dynfn-this-globalthis-001 locks identity, property write-through, the param-bearing shape and the arrow shape byte-equal vs bun

fix: delete stops misreading the void fold as a bare name, and a string receiver joins the delete kernel - the 13.5.1.1 early error is a syntax judgement so the source form decides: void <literal> folds to the undefined Ident in the arena and delete void 0 arrived identical to the user-written delete undefined, tripping the bare-name SyntaxError (the L3b case from the rotation-366 decision sweep); an operand that opens with the void token was never an IdentifierReference and answers true. The second half admits Type::String through receiver_admits_delete: 13.5.1.2 ToObject over a string primitive gives the wrapper a non-configurable own face per 10.4.3, so every delete is either the module-strict refusal throw or an absent-key true - the kernel's new Str arm (bare Str cell + ShortStr, ahead of the tag match) makes the same judgement the StringWrapper arm already made through its inner view via str_own_pair, and nothing is ever removed; probes lock in-range index and length refusing with TypeError while out-of-range answers true, fixture delete-nonref-string-001 byte-equal vs bun over the whole non-reference-return-true shape list
